newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Profits at Citibank Brazil unit to double.
newsitem.headline: Profits at Citibank Brazil unit to double.

text.p: Profits at Citicorp's Citibank Brazil unit are likely to double in 1996 when compared with last year, when the bank reported a $55.7 million net profit, said the bank's president Roberto do Valle.
Most of Citibank's profits come from what the bank calls global financing, but Valle said the bank expects an increase in revenues coming from consumer banking next year.
Valle told reporters Citibank plans to strenghten consumer credit and car loans in 1997.
Citibank is also eyeing Brazil's privatizations, particularly of the telecommunications and power sectors. Valle said the bank has $1 billion available for investing in privatizations.
He said the sell-off of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, expected to begin in February, could also be an investment opportunity but he noted it depends on how the company will be privatized.

Citibank has joined a consortium to participate in the auction of a 35 percent stake in Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT). It has also joined another group of investors to bid for concessions to operate Band B frequency for cellular telephones.
